definition: statsmodels provides classical statistical models — linear and generalised regression, time series, hypothesis tests — with detailed result summaries.
details: Grew out of Jonathan Taylor’s models module for SciPy; developed since 2009 by Skipper Seabold, Josef Perktold and the community.

explainer.lead: How to install statsmodels, a first working example, and where it fits in an AI project.
explainer.createdBy: Skipper Seabold, Josef Perktold and contributors.

quickstart.python:
import statsmodels.formula.api as smf
import pandas as pd

df = pd.DataFrame({"y": [1, 3, 2, 5, 4], "x": [1, 2, 3, 4, 5]})
model = smf.ols("y ~ x", data=df).fit()
print(model.summary())

explainer.inAi: Use it when you need p-values and confidence intervals — for example to check whether an A/B test of two prompts really differs.
explainer.jsNote: statsmodels is a Python library with no official JavaScript or TypeScript package; call it from a Python service if your app is written in JavaScript.

tiers.eli5: It is a toolbox for classic statistics: you fit a model and get a full report card explaining every part of it.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers use it for linear and generalised regression, time series, and hypothesis tests, relying on the detailed summaries for diagnostics. A pitfall is that its classical focus makes it less suited to large-scale predictive modelling than dedicated ML libraries.
tiers.paperLevel: statsmodels provides classical statistical models — linear and generalised regression, time series, hypothesis tests — with detailed result summaries.
